---
title: "How Florida Votes: Exploring Our 67 Counties!"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---

When Florida holds an election for Governor, voters all across the state cast their ballots. To help organize elections and local government, the state of Florida is divided into **67 counties**—think of them like 67 puzzle pieces that fit together to make up our state!

### Who Won each County?

Every county counts the votes cast by the people who live there. In the map below:

- The **bold black line** shows the outline of the entire state of **Florida**.
- The **white lines** inside show each of Florida's **67 counties**.
- **Red counties** had a **Republican** candidate win the most votes in that county.
- **Blue counties** had a **Democratic** candidate win the most votes in that county.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# Extract the county files to a temporary directory and read them all in
files <- unzip("2026-pri-outputofficial.zip", exdir = tempdir())
raw_data <- read_tsv(
  files,
  col_names = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(.default = "c", X19 = "d")
)

# Find the top vote-getting gubernatorial candidate in each county
county_winners <- raw_data |>
  filter(X12 == "Governor", X16 %in% c("REP", "DEM")) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(X19, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(X2, X15, X16)) |>
  slice_max(votes, n = 1, by = X2) |>
  mutate(
    county_key = str_to_lower(X2),
    winner_label = case_when(
      X15 == "Byron Donalds" ~ "Byron Donalds (Republican - 39 counties)",
      X15 == "Jay Collins" ~ "Jay Collins (Republican - 15 counties)",
      TRUE ~ "David Jolly & Gwen Graham (Democrat - 13 counties)"
    )
  )

# Load Florida county boundaries and join with the election winners
fl_counties <- counties("FL", cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  mutate(county_key = str_to_lower(NAME)) |>
  left_join(county_winners, by = "county_key")

# Create a single boundary outline for the entire state of Florida
fl_state_outline <- st_union(fl_counties)

# Map county winners like puzzle pieces inside the state of Florida
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = fl_counties,
    aes(fill = winner_label),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = fl_state_outline,
    fill = NA,
    color = "#1a1a1a",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Most Votes in the County",
    values = c(
      "Byron Donalds (Republican - 39 counties)" = "#e63946",
      "Jay Collins (Republican - 15 counties)" = "#ff8fa3",
      "David Jolly & Gwen Graham (Democrat - 13 counties)" = "#1d70b8"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Florida's 67 County Puzzle: Who Got the Most Votes?",
    subtitle = "Each puzzle piece is one county inside the state of Florida",
    caption = "Source: Florida Department of State & U.S. Census Bureau"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f8f9fa", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#d8f3fc", color = NA),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(t = 10, b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )
```

### Total Votes Across All 67 Counties (Republican Primary)

When we add up the votes from all 67 counties together, we get the statewide total! Here is how many votes each candidate received across the whole state in the Republican primary for Governor:

```{r}
# Filter to the Republican primary for Governor and sum votes by candidate
gov_rep <- raw_data |>
  filter(X12 == "Governor", X16 == "REP") |>
  summarize(votes = sum(X19, na.rm = TRUE), .by = X15) |>
  rename(candidate = X15)

# Plot a horizontal bar chart ordered by vote total
gov_rep |>
  ggplot(aes(x = votes, y = fct_reorder(candidate, votes))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#e63946") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Florida Republican Primary Results for Governor",
    subtitle = "Statewide vote totals added up from all 67 counties",
    x = "Total Votes",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Florida Department of State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```
